overview: This concurrent resolution, which needed approval from both the Senate and the House but does not go to the President, allows Emancipation Hall in the Capitol Visitor Center to be used on June 7, 2026, for an event celebrating the birthday of King Kamehameha I. Kamehameha I united the Hawaiian Islands under one rule in the early 1800s, and his birthday is a state holiday in Hawaii. The Architect of the Capitol, the office that manages the Capitol buildings, sets the conditions for setting up the event. Both chambers had approved it as of April 20, 2026.
for: Supporters say it lets the Capitol host a celebration of an important figure in Hawaiian history and culture.
against: Critics say there is little to object to, since it only approves use of a Capitol space for one event and doesn't change any law or spending.
